title: A place to think, build, and explain
summary: The purpose of this portfolio, and the standard I want each technical explanation to meet.

body.text: This portfolio begins with a simple aim: make my learning useful and inspectable. I want to connect explanations of AI concepts with working code, diagrams, experiments, and an honest account of what I still do not understand.

A technical article should do more than introduce a tool. It should explain the problem, show how the system fits together, and provide an example that someone else can reproduce. When there are tradeoffs, I want to make those visible.

items: Define a concrete problem and a baseline.
Explain the architecture and the choices behind it.
Link the implementation and describe how to run it.
Measure behavior and document failure cases.
Record limitations and the next question to investigate.

body.text: Longer articles will sit alongside short learning notes and project records. GitHub holds the source so that the work stays portable. This first entry describes the intention of the space; technical results will be added as the experiments are completed.

The portfolio uses a small static build process. Content files and public assets live together in the repository. A Node.js script turns those files into HTML pages and a writing feed. Automated checks verify the result before it is used for hosting.

body.alt: Content files and public assets feed a Node.js build, which produces static pages checked by automated tests before hosting.
body.caption: One repository, one build, and a portable output directory.

body.text:
npm run check
# Build the website, then run the automated checks.

npm run dev
# Open the local preview at http://127.0.0.1:4321

This approach keeps the initial site simple and avoids a database or account system. The tradeoff is that publishing happens by editing files and rebuilding, rather than through an online editor. Hosting and a private message service are separate decisions still to be made.
